analysis: Documentation-only PR. docs/architecture/hardware-support.md updates a date and the Nemotron Super media-charge figures: the image charge goes from 3.62 to 4.67 GiB, the video maximum from 3.49 to 4.54 GiB, and the 16-image total from 24.5 to 25.6 GiB. The charge now includes an ingress quote for a 40 MiB body. docs/architecture/inference.md updates a date and raises the Super encoded-body limit from 8 MiB to 40 MiB, with over-limit requests returning `media_too_large` (400). In the 40 MiB paragraph (inference.md head lines ~128-132) the video prompt over the context still returns the invalid-media 400. Media memory is still reserved from the shared budget before decoding, and an over-budget charge still returns 503. One image request per owner is still enforced (429 for a concurrent one). The documented limit changes are therefore not an obvious new weakening of admission, since the charge scales up with the larger body. Relevant threats are T-041 and the DoS/availability aspects of TB-007. The prefix cache, encryption, attestation and authorization (TB-011, T-053) are not touched. The unchanged Cross-repository agreement section still notes that provider quotations and platform admission must stay compatible, and this PR does not alter the capacity wire fields. I could not see the Swift source behind `maximumEncodedBodyBytes` and `mediaChargeBytes`, because only the docs are in the supplied patch. So whether the code actually enforces the 40 MiB bound and the charge before decode is unverified. The PR contains no code line to cite, so no finding. A reviewer of the companion code change should confirm the ingress check runs before base64 decoding and that the larger bodies are covered by the memory reservation. The inference.md patch excerpt is truncated, but the visible hunks are consistent.
